newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt firms despite weaker foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt firms despite weaker foreign markets.

text.p: Swedish debt yields closed lower and the crown firmed despite weaker foreign markets. Dealers said the tone of the market remained positive.
"We tracked foreign markets up. But as soon as we had a recoil buyers found their way into the market," one dealer said.

Six-month T-bill rates fell one basis point to 4.73 percent and nine-year bond yields dropped two basis points to 7.37 percent. The crown firmed to 4.3385 against the D-mark compared to 4.3480 late on Friday, which lent support to the bond market.
With little data due out in Sweden this week, the market is expected to focus on international trends.
"EU convergence looks set to continue, with Swedish bonds posting further out-performance versus bunds," U.S. investment bank PaineWebber said in its daily note.
The spread between Swedish and German long yields narrowed four basis points to 127.
"I think the spread might fall to 100 basis points but the big test comes when we start seeing signs of an improvement in the German economy," James McKay, analyst at PaineWebber told Reuters.
